Blogs

Making sense of use rate: New mobile monetization study from AdColony

Use rate is the percentage of daily active users who are served an ad at least once a day. Higher use rates lead to higher ad ARPDAU (average revenue per daily active user), which means more revenue for publishers. This new study from AdColony makes sense of use rate for mobile developers and highlights its importance as a monetization tool.

How to Start a Mobile Game Company…With Business in Mind

If you’re working on your first game, it’s worth realizing that you’re also working on your first business. This quick guide walks you through formalizing your business, testing the waters and selling people on your concept. The best tip perhaps is that when in doubt, do some research.

Using Comic Strips for Cut-scenes in my iOS Game

Martin Drapeau wrote a great piece on his tumblr that was also featured on Gamasutra this week. He gives his take on using comic strips to break up gameplay and how to create these comics for yourself. Once you’ve sketched, colored, animated and added sound to your comic, it’s ready to be added to your game. Martin also includes a great video example for you to get a better idea of what he means.

These 9 Monetization Mistakes Might Not Seem Harmful, but They Can Ruin the Success of Your Mobile Apps and Games

In a mobile world full of monetization advice and tips, it’s important to know your stuff. Rob McCardy gives his indie dev perspective on what to avoid and why. His best advice is to use a different strategy on iOS and Android. He also gives some insight into his preferences for different ad types.

How celebrity endorsements work in the Japanese mobile game market

Although most of us are now used to Kate Upton being the face of “Game of War: Fire Age”, Japanese gamers have been experiencing these celebrity endorsements for a few years now. The surge in popularity of these endorsements is due to their proven track record as a user acquisition method. According to David McCarthy, from Cybird Inc, having a celebrity endorsement can also improve your user retention.

Monetization Strategy: Redesigning Your Mobile Game From Paid to F2P

If you’re premium game isn’t doing as well as you’d like, you might considering switching to a freemium model. Soomla have put together a guide on making the change and go over the three main problems you’ll have to get over to be successful.

News

Nintendo’s first mobile game sounds weird, has in-app payments

Nintendo have announced their first mobile game, Miitomo, will be delayed until March 2016. Miitomo will be a free to play game and will include an avatar that can act of it’s own volition. After this, Nintendo intend to release 5 premium mobile games by March 2017. The release of Miitomo has been delayed in order to facilitate a global launch.

“The very low end of mobile development is likely to go away”

In a one-on-one with Kabam President, Aaron Loeb, Matthew Handrahan got his take on the future for mobile game studios. Due to changes in the market place, Loeb thinks that the core strength of studios must now be reliability rather than speed. He also predicts shifts in the market will make it harder than ever to crack the industry, “There’s so much competition, and so much quality product being created, that it will be very, very hard for those games. Harder than it has ever been.”

Google brings gameplay recording to Android with update to the Play Games app

Google have launched gameplay recording for their Android platform. You can now record yourself playing and upload it to Youtube. This seems to have come as a result of Google realizing that 3 out of 4 Android users are gamers. With this new feature 3 out of 4 users can now also become content creators. This feature works on all Android games and doesn’t require users to install any extra apps.
